package_info.why_malicious: The package deploys a Windows executable that steals browser-stored credentials and exfiltrates them to a remote server. It was intentionally crafted to mimic legitimate packages, and its installation results in full system compromise.

execution_context.file_location: main JavaScript file (likely index.js or a similar entry point in the package)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime or postinstall, the code executes a bundled Windows executable (extension.exe) that extracts browser-stored credentials, writes them to out.html, then reads and exfiltrates the file's contents via HTTP POST to a remote server, and finally deletes the evidence.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code executes a bundled binary, collects sensitive data, exfiltrates it to an external server, and deletes traces—all without user consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages do not execute binaries or exfiltrate user data. Legitimate packages should not access browser credentials or perform network exfiltration.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: A legitimate installer might run a binary for setup, but would not exfiltrate sensitive data or delete evidence.
key_indicators: Execution of a bundled Windows executable
Exfiltration of data to a hardcoded remote server
Use of child_process and network modules together

attack_chain.action: Upon installation or execution, the package runs a bundled Windows executable (extension.exe) using child_process.exec.
The executable extracts browser-stored credentials and writes them to out.html.
attack_chain.leads_to: Preparation of sensitive data for exfiltration

attack_chain.action: The JavaScript code reads out.html and sends its contents to a hardcoded remote server via HTTP POST.
The code deletes out.html to remove evidence of the theft.

behavioral_signatures: Execution of bundled Windows executables from npm packages
Access to browser credential storage files
Immediate network POST requests to hardcoded external servers after file creation
Deletion of files immediately after network exfiltration
file_indicators: out.html created and deleted in quick succession
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for execution of bundled binaries, especially those that access browser credential stores. Flag any package that sends data to hardcoded external servers or deletes files immediately after network activity. Look for the presence of suspicious executables (e.g., extension.exe) and transient files (e.g., out.html) in node_modules directories.
